research_mode: official primary sources only; police open-data, ONS crime methodology and Home Office outcome-methodology gates; no parcel result, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police open-data monthly frequency
verified_claims: Crime, anti-social behaviour and outcomes data are published with a monthly frequency.
limitations: Monthly publication does not guarantee that every force supplied complete data for every month.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police open-data geographic coverage
verified_claims: The crime and ASB dataset covers England, Wales and Northern Ireland.
limitations: Coverage does not imply identical completeness, categories or outcome availability across jurisdictions.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police open-data licence
verified_claims: The data is published under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
limitations: The licence does not remove privacy, attribution or fitness-for-purpose obligations.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Archive recency boundary
verified_claims: Except for the latest archive, historical archive snapshots are marked as out of date and the site recommends current custom-download data for most uses.
limitations: An archive snapshot must not be presented as the current state without checking its publication month.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Reported-by and falls-within fields
verified_claims: The CSV identifies the force that reported the crime and currently uses the same force for the falls-within field, while noting this may change.
limitations: The fields must not be treated as a permanent or independently verified geographic relationship.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Anonymised crime coordinates
verified_claims: Published longitude and latitude are anonymised coordinates rather than the exact incident location.
limitations: The coordinates must not be used for parcel, address or premises-level attribution.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: LSOA from anonymised point
verified_claims: Published LSOA code and name refer to the LSOA containing the anonymised map point.
limitations: The LSOA can differ from the LSOA of the true incident location and must not be treated as exact.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Crime category mapping
verified_claims: Home Office offence codes are assigned into published crime categories before release.
limitations: A broad category does not preserve the full legal offence code or case circumstances.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Latest outcome category field
verified_claims: The CSV last-outcome category represents the most recent outcome associated with the crime.
limitations: A latest outcome is not the full case history and may later be revised.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Persistent crime identifier anonymisation
verified_claims: The offence reference is replaced with a one-way hash and exposed as Crime ID or persistent_id.
limitations: The hash is not a police case reference and must not be reversed or treated as personally identifying.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Crime date month truncation
verified_claims: The incident date is truncated to year and month before publication.
limitations: The published month cannot support day-level sequencing or precise temporal attribution.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Fourteen-category classification
verified_claims: Home Office offence codes are grouped into one of 14 published categories.
limitations: Category aggregation can conceal materially different offences and should not be used as a legal classification.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Anonymous snap-point types
verified_claims: Anonymous map points are selected over road centres, public places or commercial premises.
limitations: The displayed place label does not mean the incident occurred at that named place.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Snap-point address threshold
verified_claims: Each anonymous map point has a catchment containing at least eight postal addresses or no postal addresses.
limitations: The threshold reduces privacy risk but does not create address-level accuracy.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Nearest snap-point replacement
verified_claims: Forces' exact locations are replaced with the coordinates of the nearest approved anonymous map point.
limitations: Spatial distance between the true incident and published point is not supplied and must not be assumed negligible.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Twenty-kilometre location failure rule
verified_claims: If the nearest anonymous map point is more than 20 kilometres away, published coordinates are zeroed.
limitations: Zero coordinates indicate an anonymisation or mapping boundary, not an incident at latitude or longitude zero.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Anonymous-point refresh
verified_claims: The anonymous snap-point list created in 2012 was refreshed in 2022 using newer source data.
limitations: A refreshed point list still does not represent exact incident locations or all later development.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Automated publication tests
verified_claims: Automated checks include non-empty and unique CSV tests, month-to-month count anomaly checks and force-boundary coordinate checks.
limitations: Passing automated checks does not prove that every source record is substantively correct.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Data anomaly escalation
verified_claims: Detected anomalies are flagged to the Single Online Home National Digital Team for investigation.
limitations: An investigation flag does not prove correction, completeness or the absence of other issues.

sources.publisher: Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Stop-and-search publication privacy
verified_claims: Stop-and-search data is validated for mandatory fields, has anonymised coordinates and publishes age as an age group.
limitations: Published demographic and location fields remain approximate and must not identify an individual.
